title: Load Balancing & Reverse Proxies
summary: Load balancers distribute traffic across backends; reverse proxies terminate client connections and apply routing, TLS, and policy. L4 vs L7 choice, health checks, and algorithm selection define availability and latency.

sections.title: L4 vs L7
paragraphs: L4 balances connections/packets by IP/port — cheap and protocol-agnostic. L7 understands HTTP: path routing, header-based canaries, authn hooks, and compression. L7 costs more CPU per request.
Many architectures stack both: L4 at the edge VIP, L7 at the application gateway.

sections.title: Algorithms and health
paragraphs: Round-robin, least-conn, Maglev/consistent hashing for cache friendliness and connection stickiness. Passive checks must match real readiness — accepting connections ≠ able to serve.
Slow-start and connection draining prevent thundering herds during deploys.

sections.title: Failure domains
paragraphs: Misconfigured health checks flap backends. Retry storms from proxies amplify outages — budget retries. Timeouts must be tighter than upstream client timeouts.

sections.title: Proxy as policy point
paragraphs: Modern proxies (Envoy, Nginx, HAProxy) implement mTLS, WAF rules, rate limits, and observability. Keep business logic out of the proxy when possible.

deepDive.title: Load Balancing & Reverse Proxies — Operations
paragraphs: Operating Load Balancing & Reverse Proxies in production means defining SLIs before tuning knobs, knowing amplification costs, and rehearsing failure modes.
Prefer reversible changes, feature flags, and canaries. Measure p50/p99 and error rate under load that matches production skew.
bullets: Define capacity from the scarcest resource
Keep rollback cheaper than forward repair when possible

deepDive.title: Load Balancing & Reverse Proxies — Failure modes
paragraphs: Common failures around Load Balancing & Reverse Proxies include overload, partial dependency outages, and silent correctness bugs that pass happy-path tests.
Inject faults in staging: latency, loss, clock skew, and disk full. Verify alerts fire and degradation is intentional.

expert.title: Load Balancing & Reverse Proxies — Expert notes
paragraphs: At the expert level, Load Balancing & Reverse Proxies intersects multi-region consistency, cost envelopes, and organizational constraints (team ownership, on-call load).
Write down the non-goals. Many outages come from optimizing a metric that was never the product requirement.

pitfalls: Sticky sessions as a crutch for bad state design
keyTakeaways: Proxies are policy, not business logic
whyItMatters: Every multi-instance service needs balancing; poor LB design causes cascading failures.
reflectionQuestions: Where do retries live in your stack — and are they budgeted?
numbersToKnow: Know your p99 latency budget before adding hops
Peak load ≠ average load — plan headroom (often 2–3×)
Cross-region RTT is often ~50–150ms one way
